text: Upon my bed, night after night,
I searched for him whom my soul cherishes;
I sought him but did not find him.
I must arise now and go about the city;
in the streets and in the public squares.
I must seek him whom my soul cherishes.
I searched for him but did not find him.
The watchmen who patrol the city found me,
and I asked,
“Have you seen him whom my soul cherishes?”
Scarcely had I passed them when I found him whom my soul cherishes;
I held on to him and would not let him go until I had brought him to my mother’
s house,
and into the room of her who conceived me.
I adjure you,
O daughters of Jerusalem,
by the gazelles or by the does of the field,
that you do not awaken or stir up love until it pleases.
What is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke,
perfumed with myrrh and frankincense,
with all the scented powders of the merchant?
Behold, it is the travelling couch of Solomon;
sixty warriors around it,
of the warriors of Israel.
All of them are wielders of the sword,
expert in war;
each has his sword at his side,
guarding against the terrors of the night.
King Solomon made for himself a sedan chair from the timber of Lebanon.
He crafted its posts of silver,
its back of gold,
and its seat of purple fabric,
with its interior lovingly adorned by the daughters of Jerusalem.
Go out, you daughters of Zion,
and behold King Solomon with the crown with which his mother crowned him on the day of his wedding,
and on the day of his heart’
s delight.
